subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Robinson Crusoe was a novel popular in eighteenth-century England.
• The novel featured a fictional island known as Juan Fernández Island, described as uninhabited.
• That same century, British sailors discovered what they believed was an uninhabited island in the South Pacific.
• They called it Pitcairn Island, thinking it matched the description from the novel.
• The 'uninhabited' island actually had a small population of Polynesian settlers that the sailors had failed to detect.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the role a misconception played in the naming of a place. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The novel Robinson Crusoe featured a fictional island known as Juan Fernández Island.
choices.B: Pitcairn Island in the South Pacific was named after a fictional place, though it actually had inhabitants.
choices.C: In the eighteenth century, British sailors discovered an island in the South Pacific and called it Pitcairn Island.
choices.D: Believing it was uninhabited, British sailors called an island Pitcairn after a fictional island they thought it resembled.

explanation:
Choice D is correct. It emphasizes the misconception's role: British sailors mistakenly believed the island was uninhabited and named it after a fictional island.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. The sentence mentions a novel that featured a fictional island; it doesn't emphasize the role a misconception played in the naming of a place.
